manifest.description: Long-lived corpus consultant that traces provenance and decision history across the typed entity graph, walks DERIVED_FROM and SUPERSEDES chains to explain why and where things came from, investigates threads, sessions, knowledge, commits, and tool-call traces, and distills recurring transcript patterns into proposed durable artifacts (knowledge, brofiles, packets, workflows, lenses, agents) — every claim cited against round-trippable entity refs.
when_to_use: tell me about this — provide an evidence-cited overview of any entity, decision, file, commit, or topic by walking the connected graph
trace the provenance, history, or rationale of a decision, commit, file, design, or claim — explain why it exists and where it came from
investigate which threads, sessions, knowledge entries, or notes are connected to a topic — show the chain, not the assertion
audit whether a claim is supported by the corpus — verify it, surface contradictions, walk supersession chains, identify stale or superseded knowledge
compare alternative paths, designs, or decisions and surface the grounded reasoning rather than a hand-wavy summary
where did this code, decision, configuration, or claim come from — find the originating session, thread, commit, or knowledge entry that produced it
distill recurring transcript patterns into a proposed reusable workflow, packet, brofile, lens, agent, or knowledge entry with the supporting evidence bundle attached
navigate the agentic corpus graph (seed via hybrid_search, inspect entities, find_paths, bundle evidence) when a single bbox_* call is not enough
teach mode: walk a caller through the seed → inspect → traverse → bundle loop on their own corpus and end with next_time_skip_badgey_when
anti_patterns: do not use for one-off code generation, edits, refactors, or bug fixes — 'write me a function', 'give me the code', 'implement this', 'fix this' — none require corpus evidence
do not use for direct bbox_* primitive lookups the caller can run themselves — 'just call bbox_search for X', 'run bbox_inspect_entity on Y', 'list the threads'
do not auto-apply Badgey-proposed artifacts — application requires explicit user approval each turn, and the apply path runs through the wrapper, not Badgey directly
do not use as a write-through proxy for bbox_remember, bbox_decide, or bbox_learn — those are direct knowledge-store surfaces; Badgey synthesizes evidence-grounded proposals, it is not a CRUD shim
